digest.component_or_area: MCP and review-bot service initialization and per-operation auth/config binding
propositions: MCP and review-bot long-running processes re-read static Gerrit/GitHub/LLM/telemetry config on each operation instead of binding once at startup, allowing configuration drift and inconsistent auth state across in-progress operations
MCP inbound bearer tokens and OAuth material risk leaking into startup config, operation snapshots, logs, or child process environments rather than remaining transient request-local context

review-bot validates Gerrit/GitHub decision-bearing auth lazily inside per-job work (e.g., /rerun endpoint) instead of upfront before accepting a webhook/job, and does not forward the composed LLMRuntime to the code review adapter

Partial or rejected Langfuse/OTLP telemetry setup failures may alter operation results or introduce fallback behavior instead of failing open with no-op and preserving the underlying decision unchanged
Static environment/file config material changes are observed by running long-lived MCP/review-bot processes without restart, breaking restart-rotate semantics required by deployment policy
Revoked or missing decision-bearing auth (e.g., gerrit_bot_token) silently falls back to an alternate principal or proceeds without validation instead of failing closed before work begins
